assumptions: The continuous wheel-speed, vehicle-speed, slip-ratio computation, and PID calculation are treated as external plant/controller computations; the FSM receives the resulting slip-error signal as the input variable `slp`.
The initial state is modeled as `increase` because it is the first state named in the natural-language state list and no alternate initial state was specified.
State output assignments are encoded as `enter` actions, so each mode sets the valve and pump command variables when entered.

M1_guard_off_by_one.description: guard `>= N` mistakenly written as `>= N-1` (fires one cycle too early)

M2_wrong_transition_target.description: transition `A -> B` written as `A -> C` (wrong target state)

M3_unreachable_target.description: guard threshold set far too high (`>= 99999`), target state never reached

M4_missing_forced_transition.description: forced transition `! ...` line missing (global event ignored)

M6_wrong_effect_value.description: effect assigns wrong constant (`var = N` → `var = N+100`)

scenario_results.description: default-init probe: first empty cycle dispatches to increase with inlet command, then default slp=0.0 satisfies increase->hold and neutralizes valves.
scenario_results.name: default_init_enters_increase_then_low_slip_holds

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probe: increase must transition to hold exactly at slp=0.01 and set neutral valve and pump commands.
scenario_results.name: increase_to_hold_at_positive_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start no-fire probe: increase must remain increase when slp is just above 0.01.
scenario_results.name: increase_no_fire_above_positive_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start boundary probe: hold must not transition to increase at slp=0.01 because the guard is strictly greater than 0.01.
scenario_results.name: hold_no_fire_at_positive_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probe: hold must transition to increase when slp is greater than 0.01 and set inlet valve command k1=1.
scenario_results.name: hold_to_increase_above_positive_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start boundary probe: hold must not transition to decrease at slp=-0.01 because the guard is strictly less than -0.01.
scenario_results.name: hold_no_fire_at_negative_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probe: hold must transition to decrease when slp is below -0.01, command return valve k2=1 and pump n=500, then remain decrease while still below recovery threshold.
scenario_results.name: hold_to_decrease_below_negative_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start recovery boundary probe: decrease must transition to hold exactly at slp=-0.01 and neutralize both valves and pump.
scenario_results.name: decrease_to_hold_at_negative_boundary

evidence: NL: FSM contains states `increase`, `hold`, and `decrease`.
DSL: state increase/hold/decrease are defined under SingleWheelABSRegulator.
NL: increase sets k1=1,k2=0,n=0; hold sets k1=0,k2=0,n=0; decrease sets k1=0,k2=1,n=500.
DSL enter actions implement those exact assignments.
NL transition guards: slp <= 0.01, slp > 0.01, slp < -0.01, slp >= -0.01.
DSL transitions implement the same four guards.
findings.summary: The DSL closely matches the stated three-state hydraulic supervisor: increase, hold, and decrease states are present, each assigns the specified k1, k2, and n outputs, and all four slip-threshold transitions are encoded with the stated inequalities.

evidence: NL: continuous wheel-slip dynamics remain in the plant model.

Grounding assumption: continuous wheel-speed, vehicle-speed, slip-ratio computation, and PID calculation are treated as external plant/controller computations; FSM receives resulting slip-error signal `slp`.
Design diagnostics: nl_external_input_vars includes `slp`.
DSL: `slp` is read by guards and not written internally.
findings.summary: The discrete supervisor component is covered well. The continuous wheel-speed, vehicle-speed, slip-ratio, and PID computations are not modeled internally, but the NL allows them to remain outside the discrete FSM/plant boundary and the grounding map explicitly treats slp as an external input.

evidence: DSL: `[*] -> increase`.
Grounding assumption: initial state is modeled as `increase` because it is the first state named and no alternate initial state was specified.
NL gives the state set and transitions but does not explicitly define startup behavior.
findings.summary: The initial state is assumed to be `increase`, but the NL does not explicitly specify an initial state. This is a minor review risk rather than a fidelity failure because no contradictory initial state is stated.

evidence: NL: wheel speed and vehicle speed are used to compute slip ratio, and PID output drives the Stateflow supervisor.
DSL variables: only `slp`, `k1`, `k2`, and `n` are declared.
No PID state, wheel-speed input, vehicle-speed input, or slip-ratio computation appears in the DSL.
NL also states continuous dynamics remain in the plant model, supporting this abstraction boundary.
findings.summary: The PID/slip computation is abstracted to a single scalar `slp`. This is acceptable for the described discrete supervisor, but it means the model should not be interpreted as a full ABS controller including wheel-speed/vehicle-speed processing or PID dynamics.

evidence: Diagnostics: W_UNWRITTEN_READ_VAR for `slp`.
Diagnostics: W_UNREFERENCED_VAR for `k1`, `k2`, and `n`.
Design diagnostics external_input_role_ledger identifies `slp` as an external_input_candidate.
NL: k1, k2, and n are valve/pump actions, not guard variables.
findings.summary: The diagnostics report output variables as unreferenced and `slp` as unwritten, but this mostly reflects role separation: `slp` is an external input and k1/k2/n are pure actuator outputs. The model would be clearer if these roles were explicitly annotated if the DSL supports it.

evidence: warning_budget_exhausted is empty.
Design diagnostics show advisory_count=8 and blocking_count=0.
DSL does not add artificial transitions or assignments solely to silence W_UNWRITTEN_READ_VAR or W_UNREFERENCED_VAR.
findings.summary: No unjustified repair is evident. The advisory warnings are not force-fixed by adding artificial writes or guard dependencies, which is appropriate because `slp` is externally supplied and k1/k2/n are actuator outputs.
